Q: How to run Behat on docker from within PhpStorm A:

Set the Path to Behat executable to behat binary inside behat/behat in vendor, not in the vendor/bin:

/var/www/vendor/behat/behat/bin/behat

instead of

/var/www/vendor/bin/behat

Q: Computer programs from the point of view of CPU A:

Consider this thought experiment. Write one program and compile it twice - once with optimisations disabled and once with them enabled. Now you have two different binaries containing different instructions (since the whole point of optimisation is to rewrite the program more efficiently).

Now consider that your implementations in other languages can produce at most one of these two output binaries. Therefore we cannot expect the compiled programs to operate exactly the same way. The only thing we can be sure of (if implemented correctly) is that they produce the same observable results.

Q: Fastest way to perform shapely "difference" function on two different dataframes? A:

.overlay is fastest:

Perform spatial overlay between GeoDataFrames.

df_diff = df_city.overlay(
  df_building, 
  how="difference", 
  keep_geom_type=None, 
  make_valid=True)

Q: Why does subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) with shlex.quote() break on Windows? A:

Yes, the form you show with a list of argument words and shell=False is the recommended approach.

subprocess.run(["somecli", "eval", js_code], shell=False)

Even the shlex.quote() documentation has a big red box noting exactly what you say in the question: it's not guaranteed to be correct on Windows or on other shells that have additional syntactic extensions, and subprocess.run([...], shell=False) is a better approach.

shell=True opens you up to a wide range of bugs and security issues. It's rarely necessary, and you're usually better off using Python code to do the things you'd need a shell to do (insert variables into commands, process or manipulate command outputs.

Q: Notepad++ plugin development in C++: Cannot jump to specified line right after opening File A:

I had a problem with SCI_SETFIRSTVISIBLELINE which in my case worked only if Word-Wrap was off. This is controllable through the Scintilla API.

Retrieve the setting, set word-wrap off, do your line positioning, reinstate word-wrap setting.

Q: git repository with read only permissions A:

Another way is to edit the .git/config file so the push destination fails. (see Docs).

[remote "origin"]
    url = https://github.com/example/notes.git
    pushurl = /dev/null ; Linux Mac
    pushurl = NUL ; Windows

You can still edit the documents and would need to resolve conflicts on later pulls but wont be able to push any changes to the git.

However I don't know how foolproof that is and assume it could be bypassed.

Possibly best to go for chmod as recommended by Jan Hudec for full read-only.

Q: How to surround a variable with a Live Template? A:

The issue is the shortcut rather than the $SELECTION$ variable.

For a surround template, use Ctrl + Alt + J, not Ctrl + J. Also, on some keyboards the right Alt key is treated as Alt Gr, so PhpStorm may not detect the shortcut correctly.

Using the left Ctrl + left Alt + J should bring up the correct “Surround with Live Template” action, and $SELECTION$ will then be preserved as expected.
